narrative: The model estimated your probability of bad credit at 26%, roughly a one-in-four chance. Although that may sound low, it was above the lender’s approval threshold, so the application was denied. The most influential factor was the short requested credit duration: six months against an approved-applicant average of about nineteen months. That short term worked in your favor and lowered the assessed risk. The next most important factor was your checking account status. Your account was reported as overdrawn/negative, a situation seen in only about 12.6% of approved applicants, and this was the main factor pushing the assessment toward bad credit. The third factor was savings information. With savings unknown or none, the model did not find a positive savings record to rely on, but this factor slightly supported good credit rather than counting against you. In summary, the short loan term helped you, and the savings picture did not count against you; the key concern was the overdrawn checking account, and the overall balance of factors remained above the lender’s approval threshold. To improve your next application, bring the checking account into good standing and provide evidence of savings or a longer, stable financial record. You could also ask the lender what information would make approval more likely, and consider reapplying after correcting the account status.
